clauses.current_legal_basis: The original text of EO 11904 (41 FR 5625) states no end for this clause, and no held later order, statute text or search result revokes or supersedes it. The three selected machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession of EO 11904. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Defense Superior Service Medal with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense to a member of the Armed Forces who has rendered superior meritorious service in a position of significant responsibility with the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, a specified or unified command, a Defense agency, or another designated joint activity. It is a standing establishment and award authority with no end term, and nothing held changes it.

clauses.reason: Section 2 requires the medal to be of a design approved by the Secretary of Defense, to be awarded under his regulations, and to rank in precedence after the Medal of Honor, the Distinguished Service Cross, the Defense Distinguished Service Medal, the Distinguished Service Medal and the Silver Star Medal but before the Legion of Merit. It is a continuing delegation and precedence rule with no end term, and nothing held changes it.

research_rationale:
EO 11904 (signed February 6, 1976; 41 FR 5625, Federal Register issue of February 9, 1976) establishes the Defense Superior Service Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text: an authority paragraph, four numbered sections (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and order of precedence; one medal per person with devices for later periods; posthumous award), then the signature and filing line. The dossier inventory of four clauses covers sections 1 to 4 and I confirmed it without correction. No section has a fixed end date, sunset or ending condition, and the order revokes nothing. A search of the held texts for the number 11904 finds it only in the 1989 OFR codification snapshot, which is historical editorial text and not a current basis. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 (Table IV lists it at a note preceding section 1121) with no ending statement; those are machine pointers without held statutory text, and I do not rely on them as the basis. The three selected searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no amendment, revocation or supersession of EO 11904. Every clause is therefore operative on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.

savings.reason: EO 11904 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and no held later order revokes or replaces it, so no residual effect arises. The regulations authorized by section 2 and the devices in section 3 are continuing authorizations, not accrued rights.
